title: Collapse the planning boundary to a single mutation-session contract
description:
A single mutation-session combinator and a fully typed error boundary replace the copy-pasted capture/plan/apply/retry convention and the stringify-then-downcast error handling in the transactional repository-materialization subsystem.

## Background

An adversarial audit of the repository-materialization epic (implementation grade B+, maintainability C+; recorded in `dev/studies/cdc840ad-audit-2026-07-23.md`) found that the claimed "single planning boundary" is in fact seven public plan-producing entry points across five error types. The capture/plan/apply/retry protocol is hand-copied at 30 sites across 16 command files (29 `for _ in 0..8` loops plus `commands/template.rs:176`) with 65 bespoke `Err(RetryableConflict{..}) => continue` arms and 30 distinct "did not converge" messages; only `template.rs` names its bound. Typed errors round-trip through `RepositoryStateError::Producer(String)` (34 sites) and are re-typed by the runtime downcast chain in `projection_producer` (`repository_state/mod.rs:590-598`), so exit-code correctness depends on a downcast that silently degrades when a new producer error type appears. The transaction kernel bridges two hand-aligned 4-variant action enums (`RepositoryAction` and `RepositoryJournalActionKind`) with five `unreachable!` panic sites in `storage/file_transaction.rs` that fire mid-publication, after a journal exists. Two of the five `MaterializationRequest` variants (`Initialize`, `ApplyProfile`) return early and never reach the shared plan-identity tail.

The retry sites split into 22 pure single-session loops and 8 self-managed multi-session loops that release a preflight session and then take a `.git/jit` claims guard or run an external subprocess before opening the apply session; a session held across that between-session work would invert lock ordering into a deadlock, so the contract owns the retry bound and conflict classification without holding a session across the closure.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A single mutation-session combinator owns the capture/plan/apply/retry protocol — the retry bound, conflict classification, and the terminal conflict error live in one place, and command modules contain no hand-written retry loops or per-site conflict arms. The 30 `for _ in 0..8` loops, 65 `RetryableConflict` arms, and 30 bespoke convergence messages across the 16 command files are retired.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every public plan-producing entry point returns a typed error, and producer failures reach exit-code mapping through typed variants with no stringify-then-downcast round-trip. No function in `crates/jit/src/repository_state/` carries an `anyhow` type in its signature, no error value is constructed with `format!`, and `main.rs` maps producer failures through an exhaustive match with no fallback arm.
- [hard] REQ-03: Journal-action extraction in the transaction kernel is total; the publication path contains no `unreachable!` panic sites. The five sites in `storage/file_transaction.rs` (`:759,1079,1088,1097,1104`) return a typed action-mismatch error propagated into the existing non-interruption abort with no partial write.
- [hard] REQ-04: The initialize and profile-application request variants flow through the shared plan-identity tail, or a recorded decision item states why they are exempt.

## Notes

The refactor is behavior-preserving: the existing 35 failure-injection points and ~20 interruption tests must pass unchanged, and conflict-classification unit tests move onto the combinator. REQ-04 may resolve as a recorded exemption decision rather than a code change if the two request variants genuinely cannot share the plan-identity tail.

planning.outcome: A single mutation-session contract and a fully typed error boundary collapse the copy-pasted planning surface.

title: Convert narrated materialization guarantees into enforced tests
description:
Property-based, visibility-based, and contention tests replace narrated guarantees in the repository-materialization subsystem, and well-known repository paths become compile-time constants with repair coverage derived from the repair planner.

## Background

The adversarial audit in `dev/studies/cdc840ad-audit-2026-07-23.md` found the subsystem's strongest guarantees narrated rather than enforced. The plan-derivation core has zero property-based coverage. The cutover guard is a substring test (`tests/provenance_contract/repository_state_cutover_tests.rs:39-66`) that greps four command modules for 14 forbidden literals — defeated by reformatting or by moving a raw write one file over. `ActiveLayoutTracker` (`storage/repository_state_store.rs:79-114`), which rejects reentry under a different layout, has no concurrent test, and there is no multi-threaded stress over `open_mutation_session` contention. Well-known paths are constructed stringly at ~100 fallible `VirtualPath::data("literal")` sites, and `tests/fast_rules/derived_state_repair_tests.rs:85-108` re-lists 11 repair paths by hand paired with a loose `assert!(count >= 5)`, so a new derived target silently under-covers.

The property targets are `plan_hash` determinism under action reordering and managed-document splice round-trip. The visibility replacement tightens the in-repository writers and the `FileTransactionKernel` from `pub(crate)` to `pub(in crate::storage)` so `crate::commands` can no longer name them, retaining the deleted-module and renderer-owner assertions and one narrow retained scan of the four cutover modules for raw `std::fs` publisher calls. `VirtualPath` becomes `Cow<'static, str>`-backed so well-known paths are `pub const` associated items, and a new `repair_target_paths` introspection API on `repository_state` supplies the drift-independent set from which repair coverage is derived.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-05: Property-based tests cover plan-hash determinism under action reordering and managed-document splice round-trip.
- [hard] REQ-06: The cutover guard enforces publisher visibility restrictions instead of source-text substring matching, while the deleted-module assertions are retained.
- [hard] REQ-07: Multi-threaded contention tests cover concurrent mutation-session opening and active-layout reentry rejection.
- [hard] REQ-08: Well-known repository file paths are compile-time constants, and repair-path test coverage derives from the repair planner's own declaration rather than a hand-maintained list.

## Notes

Property tests use contract-valid generators and assert observable semantic properties, not copied constants. Contention tests use real threads over a shared `InMemoryStorage` through the public store trait, not failure injection. The suite must not add integration-test targets.

planning.outcome: Property, contention, visibility, and path tests convert narrated materialization guarantees into enforced checks.

title: Establish an artifact-backed performance contract
description:
A checked-in benchmark harness, a bulk-update session-budget fix, and the profile-backed lock-hygiene change turn every published performance figure into an artifact-backed contract.

## Background

The adversarial audit in `dev/studies/cdc840ad-audit-2026-07-23.md` found every published timing to be a single self-attested measurement with no artifact. `apply_bulk_update` (`commands/bulk_update.rs:161-197`) retains the O(n)-sessions pathology — it opens preflight and publication sessions for every filter-matched issue before knowing whether anything changes (cost 2·|matched|) — while `check_auto_transitions` already demonstrates the correct shape: a cheap Issue-local eligibility prefilter that can only skip, never authorize, plus an authoritative recheck inside the session. Meanwhile zero-byte `.lock` sidecar files accumulate without bound: `load_issue` shared-locks a `<id>.lock` sidecar on every read (`storage/json.rs:918-919`, created O_CREAT at `storage/lock.rs:286-294`, never removed), so a read-all command such as `jit query available` creates one per issue read (692 sidecars observed for 665 issues).

The lock-hygiene design was decided during planning from the committed session-cost profile `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-27ffbd2d.json`: the sidecar originates on the shared read path, so even lazy creation still grows O(issues), and the sidecar read lock is therefore eliminated. Issue JSON is published by atomic temp+rename, writers serialize on `.jit/.repo-write.lock`, and `list_issues` already holds `.index.lock` shared around its load loop, so `load_issue` can read directly (or, as defense-in-depth, take the shared lock on the existing repo-scoped `.index.lock`). The surviving fixed lock set is O(1) — roughly six files independent of issue count — and orphaned sidecars are deleted once as cleanup, not correctness.

The benchmark harness `scripts/benchmark-session-cost.sh` builds the release binary, generates a fixture repository, and times each scenario with warmup and repeated measured runs, emitting one JSON artifact at the stable path `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-<jit-commit>.json` with machine, cache-state, and corpus metadata; `session-cost-27ffbd2d.json` is the first instance and the schema template. Every published timing must cite artifact path, command name, and stat.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-09: A checked-in benchmark harness records repeated runs with machine and cache-state metadata as artifacts at a stable path, and every published timing claim traces to such an artifact.
- [hard] REQ-10: Session-open budget tests bound bulk update to eligible work, matching the guarantee already tested for automatic transitions. The bound is C·|matched issues that are not provable no-ops|, with C derived from a single-issue baseline run rather than hardcoded.
- [hard] REQ-11: The per-session cost profile is recorded as an artifact, and the lock-hygiene approach chosen from that profile is implemented so zero-byte lock files no longer accumulate without bound. The per-issue sidecar read lock is eliminated, the surviving lock set is O(1) in issue count, and orphaned sidecars are cleaned up once.

## Notes

The lock-hygiene decision is pinned by plan decision PD-1: eliminate the per-issue sidecar read lock, keep the O(1) fixed lock set, decided from `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-27ffbd2d.json`. Every `load_issue` caller must be checked before removing the sidecar lock, since a reader relying on it for more than torn-read protection would be a regression; atomic temp+rename already prevents torn reads. Budget tests count session opens via the existing `TransactionFailurePoint` probe, deterministic and machine-independent. Cache-state contract is warm-only; timings are comparable only across artifacts sharing the same measurement filesystem.

planning.outcome: A checked-in benchmark harness, a bounded session budget, and lock-hygiene make performance claims artifact-backed.

title: Clear repository-state hygiene debt and document the subsystem
description:
Feature-gating, public-surface reduction, a test-module split and renames, a contributor architecture document, and clearing the recorded advisory debt bring the subsystem's maintainability up to its implementation quality.

## Background

The adversarial audit in `dev/studies/cdc840ad-audit-2026-07-23.md` recorded maintainability debt. Test-only API ships in the public library surface: `FailurePoint`/`TransactionFailureInjector`/`NoTransactionFailures` are re-exported at `storage/mod.rs:66-68`, `test_support` (`seed_issue_fixture`) and `test_helpers` are public, and `JsonFileStorage::with_repository_state_failures` (`storage/json.rs:314`) is a public fault-injection path. Exports are dead or over-broad: `issue_draft` (`mutation.rs:1314`) has zero callers, and 13 further `pub` items have no consumer outside `repository_state`. The repository-state store carries a 3,900-line inline test module (`storage/repository_state_store.rs:1806`), and several tests are named after review rounds (`test_finding2_*`, `test_f2_*`, `test_a1_*`, `test_a5_*`) rather than `test_<function>_<scenario>`. There is no contributor architecture document for the subsystem, and `dev/architecture/core-system-design.md:198-202` still points at a non-existent `docs/storage-abstraction.md`. Four non-lock advisory-debt items remain: `output.rs:433,476`, `mcp-server/lib/tool-generator.js:161,173,179`, `docs/reference/cli-commands.md:3144`, and `scripts/test-ci-manual.sh:66-90`.

The injection seam itself is production code threaded through both storage backends, so the definitions stay unconditional; a `test-support` feature gates only their public exposure, with a `#[cfg(not(feature))] pub(crate)` twin so internal resolution never changes, and tests keep compiling through a self dev-dependency that enables the feature. The public-surface reduction resolves the audit's list as eight demotions to `pub(crate)`, four contract-pinned keeps (the `Contribution` variant payload types behind the `ProfileManifest.contributions` JsonSchema wire contract), three test-only publics (`SerializedRuleSet`/`SchemaFile`/`serialize_ruleset`) moved behind `test-support`, and one deletion. The contributor architecture document lives at `dev/architecture/repository-state-materialization.md`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-12: Test-only failure-injection and fixture surfaces are feature-gated out of the default library surface, dead exports are removed, and public items with no external consumer are demoted to crate visibility.
- [hard] REQ-13: The repository-state store's inline test module lives in a sibling file, and tests named after review rounds follow the `test_<function>_<scenario>` convention.
- [hard] REQ-14: A contributor architecture document covers the repository-state/materialization subsystem, and the stale storage-abstraction pointer in the core system design document is swept.
- [hard] REQ-15: The five advisory-debt items recorded at the predecessor epic's completion are cleared from the codebase and documentation.

## Notes

The feature gating is designed to require no CI or gate-config changes: the self dev-dependency unifies the feature into `cargo test --workspace` while release builds drop the surface, and the standalone `clippy --lib` gate verifies the feature-off public surface. Of REQ-15's five advisory-debt items, four are cleared here; the fifth — the unbounded zero-byte lock files — is cleared by the performance-contract lock-hygiene work and needs no change in this story. The store test split moves a module to a sibling file without adding integration-test targets.

planning.outcome: Feature-gating, surface reduction, test-module hygiene, docs, and debt clearance harden the repository-state subsystem.

title: Replace the repository-materialization showcase with a corrected successor
description:
A corrected successor deck retells the repository-materialization story with every falsifiable claim traced to a repository artifact, and the predecessor deck is archived behind a tombstone.

## Background

The adversarial audit in `dev/studies/cdc840ad-audit-2026-07-23.md` found nine falsifiable errors in the predecessor showcase deck (`dev/presentations/cdc840ad/talk.html`): a fabricated `fn derive(...)` signature, a non-existent "inspectable" plan JSON document, a "130 session opens" figure that is a 65-issue in-memory model prediction rather than a measurement of this repository, an "independent holistic PASS" that was written by the same agent that built the epic, a `RepositoryImage` struct with a field it does not have, and a diffstat row that reproduces under no stated path filter. It also found the deck loads reveal.js, KaTeX, and three font families from CDNs and cannot present air-gapped, while carrying KaTeX that no slide uses.

The successor deck lives at `dev/presentations/1cc809de/` and re-derives its figures from the performance artifacts and the final tree; every timing cites artifact path, command name, and stat. It carries an explicit correction inventory keyed by audit finding id (A1-1..A1-6, the A2 claims it retells, and A4-1..A4-3), mapping each to its corrected claim and evidence. It ships without KaTeX and with reveal.js and fonts vendored under the deck folder so it presents air-gapped. The predecessor deck moves to `dev/archive/features/cdc840ad/showcase`, leaving a tombstone at the original path that points to the successor deck and the audit.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-16: A corrected successor presentation of the repository-materialization story exists in which every falsifiable claim traces to a repository artifact, and the predecessor deck is archived with a tombstone pointing to the successor and the audit.

## Notes

This deck is a corrected retelling of the predecessor story, not a deck about this epic's own work. Asset vendoring is pinned by plan decision PD-2: reveal.js and fonts are vendored locally and KaTeX is dropped, so rendering is reproducible from the repository alone. The successor must pass the presentation fit checker across all slides.

planning.outcome: A corrected successor deck traces every falsifiable claim to an artifact and the predecessor deck retires behind a tombstone.

title: Single-session retry call-site migration
description:
The pure single-session capture/plan/apply/retry loops in the command layer, and the inline capture-conflict arms, adopt the shared mutation-session combinators, so no single-session site keeps a hand-written retry loop, conflict arm, or bespoke convergence message.

## Background

The command layer historically hand-copied a capture/plan/apply/retry protocol at thirty sites. Twenty-two of them are pure single-session loops: open one recovered mutation session, capture, plan, apply, and retry on a conflict. The shared contract they adopt is:

```rust
enum SessionStep<T> { Apply(MaterializationPlan, T), Done(T), Retry }

fn with_mutation_session<S: RepositoryStateStore, T>(
    store: &S, layout: &RepositoryLayout, operation: &'static str,
    attempt: impl FnMut(&mut dyn RepositoryMutationSession) -> Result<SessionStep<T>>,
) -> Result<T>;

fn capture_or_retry<T>(outcome: Result<T, RepositoryStateStoreError>) -> Result<AttemptOutcome<T>>;
```

Each single-session loop is rewritten to a `with_mutation_session` call whose closure returns `SessionStep::Apply(plan, value)` when it derives a plan, `SessionStep::Done(value)` for a read-only or already-converged path, and `SessionStep::Retry` on a capture conflict. The four sites that classify a capture conflict with an inline match arm adopt `capture_or_retry` instead. After the rewrite these sites carry no `for _ in 0..8` loop, no `RetryableConflict` match arm, and no bespoke "did not converge" message.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The pure single-session retry loops in the command modules are rewritten onto `with_mutation_session`, with read-only or already-converged paths returning `SessionStep::Done`.
- [hard] REQ-02: The inline capture-conflict arms adopt `capture_or_retry`; none of these sites retains a `for _ in 0..8` loop, a `RetryableConflict` arm, or a bespoke convergence message.
- [hard] REQ-03: The command-module behavior is unchanged: the existing failure-injection and interruption tests pass without modification.

## Notes

The self-managed multi-session sites - those that release a preflight session and then take a claims guard or run a subprocess before applying - are not migrated here; they retain their between-session structure and are converted separately. Lock ordering at every rewritten site is preserved.

planning.outcome: The pure single-session retry loops and inline capture arms move onto the shared mutation-session combinators.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Mechanical rewrite of the pure single-session loops onto the shared combinator, verified by the untouched interruption suite.

footprint.uncertainty: dependency.rs, issue.rs, gate.rs, gate_check.rs, and mod.rs also hold self-managed multi-session sites that are out of scope here; template.rs holds only a self-managed site and is not touched by this task

title: Self-managed multi-session retry migration
description:
The eight self-managed multi-session retry sites move onto the shared session-free retry driver, keeping their preflight-release-guard-apply structure and lock ordering unchanged.

## Background

Eight command sites run a multi-session retry: within one attempt they release a preflight session and then acquire a `.git/jit` claims guard, run an external checker subprocess, or revalidate a cross-reopen invariant before opening the apply session. The sites are `dependency.rs:260,396`; `issue.rs:552`; `gate.rs:1357`; `mod.rs:2141,2353`; `gate_check.rs:909`; `template.rs:176`. A retry driver that held a session across this between-session work would hold `.repo-write.lock` across `claims_mutation_guard` (inverting today's lock order into a deadlock hazard) and across multi-second subprocess runs, so these sites cannot use a session-holding convenience.

They migrate onto the session-free retry driver:

```rust
fn with_mutation_attempts<T>(operation: &'static str,
    attempt: impl FnMut() -> Result<AttemptOutcome<T>>) -> Result<T>;
enum AttemptOutcome<T> { Done(T), Retry }
```

`with_mutation_attempts` owns the retry bound and the terminal `MutationSessionExhausted` error and holds no session, so the closure opens and releases sessions, takes a claims guard, and runs a subprocess between them exactly as today. Each site keeps its present structure: preflight, release, guard/subprocess, the same cross-reopen equality checks (`template.rs:217-227`; `mod.rs:2430-2444,2491`; `gate_check.rs:997`) returning `Retry`, then apply classified through the shared apply-conflict classifier. Guards are closure locals whose `Drop` runs after apply, preserving lock ordering byte-for-byte.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The eight sites (`dependency.rs:260,396`; `issue.rs:552`; `gate.rs:1357`; `mod.rs:2141,2353`; `gate_check.rs:909`; `template.rs:176`) run their retry through `with_mutation_attempts`; none retains a `for _ in 0..8` loop, a per-site `RetryableConflict` arm, or a bespoke convergence message.
- [hard] REQ-02: The cross-reopen revalidation and lock ordering at each site are unchanged; guards drop after apply exactly as before.
- [hard] REQ-03: After this task no `for _ in 0..8` loop, no `RetryableConflict` match arm, and no bespoke "did not converge" message remains anywhere in the command modules.
- [hard] REQ-04: The existing failure-injection and interruption tests pass unchanged; behavior is preserved.

## Notes

This migration consumes the session-free retry driver and shared apply-conflict classifier; those must already exist. Lock ordering must remain byte-for-byte identical: holding `.repo-write.lock` across the claims guard or a subprocess would deadlock.

planning.outcome: The eight self-managed multi-session sites move onto the shared retry driver with lock ordering preserved.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Eight known call sites converted onto the shared driver with lock ordering preserved byte-for-byte.

title: Typed producer error family for repository-state
description:
Every plan-producing entry point in the repository-materialization module returns a typed `ProducerError`, so producer failures no longer stringify through `RepositoryStateError::Producer(String)`.

## Background

Producer failures currently stringify through `RepositoryStateError::Producer(String)` and are re-typed by a runtime downcast chain, so exit-code correctness depends on a downcast that silently degrades when a new producer error type appears. This task introduces the typed producer family and retypes the producer surfaces; the exhaustive exit-code match and the module-wide sweep of residual untyped errors are separate work.

1. New `ProducerError` (thiserror), each variant carrying its typed source: `MissingCapture(&'static str)`, `MalformedUtf8(#[from] FromUtf8Error)`, `UnknownProjection(String)`, `UnknownKind { projection, kind }`, plus transparent `#[from]` for `CaptureError`, `RepositoryLayoutError`, `ConfigurationDeclarationError`, `InvariantConfigError`, `ItemError`, `RuleConfigError`, `ProjectionError`, `ManagedDocumentError`. The six `materialize.rs` producers (`read_text`, `assemble_config`, `assemble_config_from_declarations`, `render_capture_closure`, `validate_capture_closure`, `compose_configured_projections`) and the two internal `anyhow` leaves - `render_projection_body` in `projection_render.rs` (whose injected read-closure becomes `FnMut(&str) -> Result<Option<String>, ProducerError>`) and `validate_proposed_layout` in `artifact_classifier.rs` - return `Result<_, ProducerError>`.
2. `RepositoryStateError::Producer(String)` becomes `Producer(#[from] ProducerError)`. The stringifying `producer`/`projection_producer` sink helpers and the `.map_err(...producer...)` sites in `mod.rs` are replaced with `?`. The inline `Producer(format!)` sites become `ProducerError::ConfigParse` and a new `RepositoryStateError::Overlay(#[from] OverlayError)`. The profile-application producers in `profile_apply.rs` retype with profile-specific variants - `ProfileRegistryNotFile { target }`, `ProfileRegistryParse { target, #[source] source }`, `ProfileContributionConflict { identity, registry }`.

The exit-code boundary in `main.rs` is left unchanged; the profile-target-conflict predicate keeps returning the same boolean against the typed representation so the binary still compiles. Rewriting that boundary into an exhaustive match is out of scope here.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `ProducerError` exists with the variants above, and `RepositoryStateError::Producer` carries `#[from] ProducerError`.
- [hard] REQ-02: The six `materialize.rs` producers, `render_projection_body`, and `validate_proposed_layout` return `Result<_, ProducerError>`; the stringifying producer sink helpers and their `.map_err` sites are replaced with `?`.
- [hard] REQ-03: The profile-application producers in `profile_apply.rs` return typed profile-specific variants rather than `Producer(String)`.
- [hard] REQ-04: For the surfaces retyped here, `String`-typed variant fields hold raw identifiers and message rendering lives in `Display` impls rather than `format!`-constructed values.
- [hard] REQ-05: Existing behavior and exit codes are preserved; the failure-path tests pass unchanged.

## Notes

Retyping the two finalizers and the exhaustive exit-code mapping are separate work. The profile-target-conflict predicate is retained here, adapted to the typed variant, so the exit boundary continues to compile.

planning.outcome: Producer failures carry a typed ProducerError instead of stringifying through Producer(String).

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One error type and the producer-surface retyping within the repository-state module, verified by the failure-path tests.

title: Typed finalizer errors for gate-registry edit and archive execution
description:
The two finalizers in the repository-materialization module - gate-registry edit and archive execution - return typed `RepositoryStateError` values through dedicated error types instead of stringified producer errors.

## Background

`finalize_gate_registry_edit` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs`) and `finalize_archive_execution` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/archive.rs`) reach exit mapping through untyped error values. This task gives each a typed error family composed into `RepositoryStateError`.

1. `finalize_gate_registry_edit` returns `Result<_, RepositoryStateError>` via a new `GateRegistryEditError { MissingEdit, MultipleEdits, DeclarationMismatch }` variant, with `#[from]` variants for its `?`-propagated leaf classes (`MutationError`, `GateDeclarationError`, `OverlayError`, `SeedError` join the existing `Delta`/`PlanHash`/`Layout`).
2. `finalize_archive_execution` returns `Result<_, RepositoryStateError>` via a new `ArchiveExecutionError` enumerating the archive-specific classes at their construction sites - `MissingDestination`, `MissingContentIdentity`, `ContentIdentityChanged`, `NonFileSource { role }`, `UnsafeOccupant { role }`, `MissingPlannedDocument`, `RelinkTargetsPinned`, `RelinkStale`, `MissingCapturedIssue`, `MalformedIssueJson(#[source] serde_json::Error)`, `IssueIdMismatch`, `CapturedIssueCacheLost`, `MissingChangedIssue` - plus `#[from]` for its typed leaves (`EventLogError`, `PlanError`, and the typed `validate_proposed_layout`).

`String`-typed variant fields carry raw identifiers, not pre-rendered messages; all rendering lives in `Display` impls.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `finalize_gate_registry_edit` returns a typed `RepositoryStateError` via a `GateRegistryEditError` variant with the classes above and `#[from]` compositions for its propagated leaves.
- [hard] REQ-02: `finalize_archive_execution` returns a typed `RepositoryStateError` via an `ArchiveExecutionError` variant enumerating the archive-specific classes and `#[from]` for its typed leaves.
- [hard] REQ-03: No error value in these two finalizers is constructed with `format!`; `String`-typed fields hold raw identifiers and rendering lives in `Display` impls.
- [hard] REQ-04: Existing behavior and exit codes are preserved; the finalizer failure-path tests pass unchanged.

## Notes

This work composes on the typed producer error family, since `ArchiveExecutionError` embeds the typed `validate_proposed_layout` result. The exhaustive exit-code match over `RepositoryStateError` is separate work.

planning.outcome: The gate-registry-edit and archive-execution finalizers return typed RepositoryStateError values.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Two finalizer signatures retyped through dedicated error families, verified by the finalizer failure-path tests.

title: Exhaustive exit-code mapping and residual error-string sweep
description:
The binary's exit-code mapping matches `RepositoryStateError` exhaustively with no fallback arm, and the remaining untyped error signatures across the repository-materialization module are retired.

## Background

With producer and finalizer failures typed, the exit-code boundary can stop probing by downcast. This task closes the boundary and sweeps the residual untyped surfaces module-wide.

1. `main.rs::error_to_exit_code` becomes one exhaustive match over `RepositoryStateError` with no `_ =>` arm: projection, managed-document, profile-conflict, ambiguous-ownership, gate-registry-edit, and archive-execution variants map to the validation-failed exit; capture and parse producer variants to the generic exit; layout variants to the invalid-argument exit. The profile `--json` boundary keeps its single sanctioned `downcast_ref::<RepositoryStateError>` on the anyhow CLI transport, but `profile_json_error` matches the `ProfileTargetConflict` variant (and the profile producer variants map to the profile conflict and profile error codes explicitly) instead of a boolean predicate, which is deleted.
2. The residual sweep retires the remaining `anyhow`-typed signatures and `format!`-constructed error values elsewhere in `crates/jit/src/repository_state/`, including the export, initialization, and profile-application paths, so no function in the module carries an `anyhow` type in its signature and no error value is built with `format!`.

## Success Criteria

title: Total journal-action extraction in the transaction kernel
description:
Journal-action extraction in the transaction kernel becomes total: the five `unreachable!` panic sites in the publication path return a typed action-mismatch error that propagates into the existing non-interruption abort with no partial write.

The transaction kernel bridges two hand-aligned 4-variant action enums - `RepositoryAction` (semantic intent) and `RepositoryJournalActionKind` (staging control-names) - with five `unreachable!` panic sites in `crates/jit/src/storage/file_transaction.rs` (`:759,1079,1088,1097,1104`) that fire mid-publication, after a journal exists. - The four extractor sites (`:1079-:1104`) already sit inside the prepare loop that the abort handler wraps, so `?` reaches the abort directly.

title: Cow-backed VirtualPath with well-known path constants

title: Derived repair-target coverage authority

## Background

Every family in `derive_repair` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs`) is drift-filtered - projections skip when bytes already match, the default ruleset writes only on diff, profile targets push only when the entry differs - so a set derived from walked actions would enumerate only currently-drifting paths. The eleven literals also mix repair write-targets with three fixture-input-only paths (`index.json`, `events.jsonl`, the profile record) that `derive_repair` never writes.

title: Benchmark harness and first session-cost artifact
description:
Add a checked-in benchmark harness that records repeated timing runs as JSON artifacts at a stable repository path, so every published performance figure traces to an artifact instead of a single self-attested measurement.

## Background

Today every published timing is a lone, un-artifacted measurement. This task adds `scripts/benchmark-session-cost.sh`, modeled on the existing `scripts/benchmark-rust-build.sh`. The script builds the release binary, generates a fixture repository of a recorded issue count, and times each scenario with at least 3 warmup runs and at least 20 measured runs, emitting one JSON artifact at the stable path `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-<jit-commit>.json` — the jit commit in the filename so history accumulates. The committed `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-27ffbd2d.json` is the first instance and the schema template the harness must reproduce.

Artifact schema (top-level keys): `schema_version`; `jit{version,commit,dirty,profile}`; `machine{cpu_model,logical_cpus,ram_kb,kernel,measurement_fs,repo_real_fs}`; `corpus{issue_count}`; `method{samples_per_command,warmup_runs,warm,cache_state,timing_clock}`; `commands[]{name,argv,class,n,min_ms,median_ms,p95_ms,max_ms,lock_files_created}`; and `mutation_syscall_summary{task_clock_ms,user_s,sys_s,page_faults,context_switches}`.

Scenarios in the `commands` array: baseline (`--version`), single read (`issue show`), read-all (`query available` and `issue list`), and single mutation (`issue update --priority`). The bulk-mutation scenario is intentionally excluded here; it is added later, once the bulk-update fix lands, so its numbers measure the fixed behavior.

Mutable scenarios need a reset protocol: the harness materializes a fresh fixture repository per measured sample (regenerate, or restore from a pristine copy) so no sample observes a prior sample's mutations; warmup runs use throwaway fixtures of the same shape.

Cache-state contract is warm-only: cold-cache measurement needs root to drop the page cache and is not assumed; warm means the page cache is primed by warmup runs against the pristine copy. Timings are comparable only across artifacts sharing the same `measurement_fs`.

Citation rule: every published timing must cite artifact path, command name, and stat (for example `session-cost-<commit>.json > issue_update_mutation > median_ms`); an uncited number is a staleness defect.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `scripts/benchmark-session-cost.sh` is checked in, builds the release binary, generates a fixture repository of a recorded issue count, and for each scenario runs at least 3 warmup and at least 20 measured runs, emitting one JSON artifact at `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-<jit-commit>.json`.

- [hard] REQ-03: The `commands` array covers the baseline (`--version`), single-read (`issue show`), read-all (`query available` and `issue list`), and single-mutation (`issue update --priority`) scenarios, and contains no bulk-mutation scenario.
- [hard] REQ-04: Each mutable scenario runs against a freshly materialized fixture per measured sample so no sample observes a prior sample's mutation, and warmup runs use throwaway fixtures of the same shape.
- [hard] REQ-05: The artifact records machine identity (cpu model, logical cpus, ram, kernel, measurement filesystem, real-repo filesystem) and a warm-only cache-state field.
- [hard] REQ-06: Any performance timing stated in repository prose or documentation cites artifact path, command name, and stat.

## Notes

Model the script structure on `scripts/benchmark-rust-build.sh`. Timing figures are machine-specific; record machine identity rather than asserting portability. Do not hardcode expected millisecond values in tests — the artifact is the contract, not any single number.

title: Bulk-update eligibility prefilter and session budget
description:
`apply_bulk_update` opens sessions only for matched issues that actually need a change, matching the session-budget guarantee already tested for automatic transitions.

## Background

`apply_bulk_update` (`crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs`) opens a preflight session and a publication session for every filter-matched issue before knowing whether anything changes - cost 2*|matched|. The automatic-transitions path already demonstrates the correct shape: a cheap in-memory eligibility prefilter that can only skip, never authorize, plus an authoritative recheck inside the session.

Add a pure `UpdateOperations::is_provable_noop(&Issue) -> bool` prefilter over the already-listed issues. It is Issue-local and no-op-only: it skips an issue exactly when every operation's target value already holds (state equal, labels present or absent, priority, gate and assignee state), all decidable from the listed `Issue` alone. Potentially invalid updates are not prefiltered - they still open sessions so the same authoritative in-session validation produces the same per-issue error results as before; repository-dependent validity never moves out of the session, and the prefilter only skips, never authorizes.

The session-open bound is C*|matched issues that are not provable no-ops|, where C is the per-mutation session constant (currently 2: preflight plus publication). The budget test derives C from a single-issue baseline run rather than hardcoding it, counts session opens via the existing once-per-session-open failure-point probe, seeds K matched issues of which K-J already hold their target values, and asserts C*J session opens.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `apply_bulk_update` opens sessions only for matched issues that are not provable no-ops; for K matched issues of which J require a change, session opens equal C*J where C is the per-mutation session constant.
- [hard] REQ-02: `UpdateOperations::is_provable_noop` is a pure, Issue-local predicate that skips an issue exactly when every operation's target value already holds; it never authorizes an update and never moves repository-dependent validity out of the session.
- [hard] REQ-03: An issue whose update is potentially invalid still opens a session and yields the same per-issue error result as before the change.
- [hard] REQ-04: The session-budget test derives C from a single-issue baseline run, counts session opens via the existing once-per-session-open failure-point probe, and asserts C*J for K seeded issues with K-J already at their target values.

## Notes

The change is behavior-preserving for update results: only the number of sessions opened for provable no-ops changes. Do not hardcode C; a single-issue baseline run yields it. Recording a bulk-mutation scenario in the benchmark harness is separate work.

planning.outcome: Bulk update opens sessions only for matched issues that are not provable no-ops.

title: Lock-hygiene: eliminate the per-issue sidecar read lock
description:
Eliminate the per-issue sidecar read lock so zero-byte `.lock` files no longer accumulate without bound, keep the surviving fixed lock set O(1) in issue count, and clean up orphaned sidecars once.

## Background

Zero-byte `.lock` sidecar files accumulate without bound. `load_issue` takes a shared lock on a `<id>.lock` sidecar on every read (`crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs`, around lines 918-919), created with `O_CREAT` at `crates/jit/src/storage/lock.rs` (around lines 286-294) and never removed. A read-all command such as `jit query available` therefore creates one sidecar per issue read (692 sidecars observed for 665 issues).

The pinned decision (PD-1) is to eliminate the per-issue sidecar read lock. It is redundant: issue JSON is published by atomic temp-file-plus-rename, so a reader can never observe a torn file; writers serialize on `.jit/.repo-write.lock`; and `list_issues` already holds the repo-scoped `.index.lock` shared around its load loop. `load_issue` can therefore read directly, or, as defense-in-depth, take the shared lock on the existing repo-scoped `.index.lock` instead of a per-issue sidecar. The surviving fixed lock set is O(1) — roughly six files independent of issue count (`.repo-write`, `.index`, `.gates`, `.events`, the per-worktree bootstrap lock, and the claims lock). Retained fixed locks stay `O_CREAT` without `O_EXCL` and are never unlinked, so flock coordination remains race-safe. Orphaned sidecars are deleted once as cleanup, not correctness.

Every existing `load_issue` caller must be checked before removing the lock: a reader that relied on the sidecar for more than torn-read protection would be a regression, and atomic temp-plus-rename already prevents torn reads.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The per-issue sidecar read lock in `load_issue` is eliminated; no read path creates a per-`<id>.lock` sidecar file.
- [hard] REQ-02: After a command that reads every issue, the number of lock files that exist is O(1) in issue count — the surviving fixed lock set is independent of the number of issues.
- [hard] REQ-03: Orphaned zero-byte sidecar `.lock` files are removed once as a cleanup step.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every existing `load_issue` caller is confirmed not to depend on the sidecar lock for anything beyond torn-read protection, which atomic temp-file-plus-rename already provides.
- [hard] REQ-05: This clears the outstanding zero-byte-lock advisory-debt item.

## Notes

The per-session cost profile artifact half of this contract is already committed at `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-27ffbd2d.json`; do not regenerate or duplicate it here. Retained fixed locks must keep their current `O_CREAT`-without-`O_EXCL` creation and must not be unlinked, so flock coordination stays race-safe.

planning.outcome: Removing the per-issue sidecar read lock keeps the surviving fixed lock set O(1) in issue count.

title: Feature-gate the test-support library surface
description:

## Background

A `test-support` feature in `crates/jit/Cargo.toml` gates each of these public exposures, in every case keeping a feature-off twin so nothing inside the crate changes how it resolves the symbol:

- The sole public re-export of `FailurePoint as TransactionFailurePoint`, `TransactionFailureInjector`, and `NoTransactionFailures` at `crates/jit/src/storage/mod.rs:66-68`. Under the feature it stays `pub use`; without it, a `#[cfg(not(feature = "test-support"))] pub(crate) use` twin exposes the same names crate-internally so internal callers resolve identically.
- `mod test_support` (the `seed_issue_fixture` helper, which uses `.expect()` calls unfit for shipped library code).
- `pub mod test_helpers`, currently `#[cfg(test)]` at `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:64`, widened to `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]`.
- The conflict-injection branch at `crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store.rs:527-532` plus its `memory.rs` backing machinery: change `#[cfg(test)]` to `#[cfg(feature = "test-support")]`.
- The file backend's only public fault-injection path, `JsonFileStorage::with_repository_state_failures` at `crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:314`, with the same feature-on-`pub` / feature-off-`pub(crate)` twin.

The memory backend's injection twins are already `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate)` and need no change.

Tests keep compiling through a self dev-dependency: add `[dev-dependencies] jit = { path = ".", features = ["test-support"] }` to `crates/jit/Cargo.toml`, and enable the same feature on `crates/server`'s `jit` dev-dependency. This unifies the feature into `cargo test --workspace` while `cargo build` and release builds drop the surface. No integration-test target is added, and no CI or gate configuration changes.

With the feature disabled, none of `TransactionFailurePoint`, `TransactionFailureInjector`, `NoTransactionFailures`, `seed_issue_fixture`/`test_support`, `test_helpers`, or `JsonFileStorage::with_repository_state_failures` is reachable from the crate's public API (each is `pub(crate)`, `#[cfg]`-excluded, or otherwise non-`pub`).
